title: Interlock runbook for PRD acceptance when KV-cache behavioral experiments alter API/contract
creator: Sofia Chen
description:
Background: The runtime team will roll out an experimental KV-cache behavior that can change response determinism for long-chat sessions under certain prefix-caching heuristics. This ticket defines the cross-team interlock: how Product, Engineering, Design, and Legal coordinate PRD acceptance and sign-offs when the change touches API stability, user-facing behavior, and contractual commitments.

Scope: Produce an interlock runbook and checklist covering: 1) deterministic acceptance criteria for feature parity vs baseline, 2) explicit rollback/mitigation triggers tied to telemetry thresholds, 3) legal / TOS assessment for non-deterministic outputs and customer notice language, 4) design guardrails for UX indicating degraded determinism, and 5) an owner matrix and SLA for sign-off turnaround during the staged rollout.

Outcome: A single-page acceptance runbook attached to the PRD, a staged sign-off cadence (canary -> regional -> global), and documented handover tasks for support/CS if customer incidents arise.
acceptance_criteria: PRD updated with a clear description of altered KV-cache semantics and user-visible behavioral delta
Engineering provides a telemetry plan with concrete thresholds (error-rate, perplexity drift, repeatable regression tests) that map to rollback/hold actions
Design supplies microcopy and UI states for 'best-effort' determinism and confirms no misleading guarantees
Legal reviews and signs off on customer-facing language and confirms no contract breach; legal note added to PRD
Each staging phase has at least one named approver from Eng, Design, PM, and Legal; sign-offs are recorded in the PRD and on the rollout ticket
Runbook includes post-release monitoring dashboard links and an on-call playbook for immediate mitigation
Backout plan validated in a dry-run with DevOps and has < 2 hour estimated revert time documented
